text: Here's how to write a check, like you're five.
A check is a note to your bank that says: please give this person my money.
Spot one, top right: today's date.
Spot two: who gets the money. Write their name.
Spot three: the amount in numbers. Squeeze it right up against the dollar sign,
so this sneaky raccoon can't sneak an extra number in.
Spot four: the same amount, in words. Twenty five, and fifty over one hundred.
Then draw a line to the end, so nobody can add more.
Secret: if the words and the numbers don't match, the bank usually trusts the words.
Spot five, the memo: a little note that says what it's for. It's optional.
Spot six, the big one: sign your name. No signature, no money.
Always use a pen, and never sign a blank check. That's like handing the raccoon your piggy bank.
The numbers at the bottom are your bank's name tag and your account number. Leave them alone.
Six spots, and you just wrote a check. Which spot didn't you know?
Follow for more grown-up stuff, explained like you're five.
So next time someone says, just write me a check...
